sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles a short stretch of the southern Apennines between the Basilicata and Calabria regions, across of the high Sinni R. valley, on the western flank of Mt. Pollino. This Source is a high-angle, NE-dipping, normal fault system along the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a sparse distribution of intermediate and damaging seismicity nearby this region: to the northwest, the 2 January 1831 (Mw 5.5, Lagonegro), and 20 November 1836 (Mw 5.8, Basilicata meridionale) earthquakes have occurred, while the southeastern sector has been affected by the 9 September 1998 (Mw 5.7, Appennino Calabro-Lucano), and 26 January 1708 (Mw 5.6, Pollino) events.
This Source can be seen as the southernmost reach of the greater NW-SE striking extensional axis of the southern Apennines, just before the Calabrian Arc to the south of Mt. Pollino. Field data by Schiattarella et al. (1994) and by De Martini (1996) suggest the existence of the Mercure fault in the southern sector of the source, that has been interpreted as an area of seismic gap.
The main segment of this Source has been recognized for its seismogenic potential. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents pure extension, based on geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological data. The slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
